correctness.rationale: The theorem is quantified for every fixed nondegenerate two-dimensional increment covariance. Exact endpoint comparisons show F<=epsilon forces both Brownian differences below 3epsilon with bounded endpoints. The reverse strict event sup X_j<epsilon/2 and each terminal X_j in (0,epsilon/4) has F<epsilon. Whitening gives a wedge with angle arccos(-rho). An explicit uniformly convergent Dirichlet Bessel expansion yields an O(epsilon^(2+2beta)) upper estimate on bounded wedge endpoints and a strictly positive lower coefficient on the interior rectangle. Combining gives the sharp power; exact covariance algebra, 700 finite path checks and 15 high-precision kernel checks corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 source provides the sharp candidate exponent as a necessary cone-confinement upper bound for rho<-1/2, but neither a positive lower bound nor a theorem over all nondegenerate correlations. The present proof supplies a positive-area interior terminal confinement whose wedge survival has the same exponent. Equivalence checks, stronger-coverage comparisons and targeted research-index searches found no result implying this complete two-sided statement; risks from unindexed reformulations and incompletely accessible historic cone papers remain.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased small-deviation theorem may combine classical wedge heat kernels with the same sufficient confinement condition.
The historical cone paper and the 2015 wedge-survival paper were not independently inspected in full text; their general cone events alone do not directly give the last-passage event comparison.
The isotropic rho=-1/2 exponent is compatible with prior traceless GUE results and is not independently novel.

value.rationale: The natural three-state Markov-word Brownian RSK limit had only a one-sided high-order lower-tail bound for anisotropic correlations. The theorem determines its sharp logarithmic rare-event exponent across all nondegenerate covariances, giving an exact quantitative invariant at the cyclic boundary rho=-1/2 and a concrete noncyclic value 18.5237748...; this is a motivated sharp distributional law, not a technical restatement of the old upper bound.
